subject.title: fix(copilot): bound BYOK proxy request bodies

question: Should OpenClaw impose one universal 16 MiB aggregate body cap and 30-second total-read deadline on every Copilot BYOK provider request?
rationale: The pinned SDK does not define those universal boundaries, and choosing aggregate size plus total-duration semantics determines which previously supported provider and multimodal requests will fail after upgrade.

options.title: Calibrate a conservative envelope
options.body: Choose limits and timeout semantics from representative text, tool, multimodal, and slow-upload requests, then update the focused tests and proof.

options.title: Accept 16 MiB / 30 seconds
options.body: Intentionally own the proposed rejection boundary after documenting and proving representative supported workloads fit inside it.

options.title: Pause fixed limits
options.body: Keep the PR open until upstream guidance or measured workload evidence supports a safe universal policy.

recommendation.title: Calibrate a conservative envelope
recommendation.body: Choose limits and timeout semantics from representative text, tool, multimodal, and slow-upload requests, then update the focused tests and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Copilot BYOK proxy and are the strongest feature-history owner for its supported provider request contract.
